tmp:2727: "You shall set an opening in the darkness in which you are trapped" — homiletic reading of the ark's side-door (petach ha-teivah) as making an exit of truth from one's darkness/obstacle
tmp:2728: Tishrei — the month of the High Holidays, identified with holy boldness (azut di-kedushah), called 'yerach ha-eitanim' (month of the mighty)
tmp:2729: "You will prevail over your enemies" — the state of overcoming foes achieved through love/chesed ('many waters cannot extinguish the love')
tmp:2730: "The melody will be elevated and perfected" — future messianic perfection of neginah within the da'at of holy Malkhut when God is King over all the earth
tmp:2732: "He can make Rosh Hashanah" — the tzaddik's capacity to enact/create the Day of Judgment itself, an action-power derived from holiness
tmp:2733: The Throne of Glory (Kisei ha-Kavod) as the root-source of souls — kabbalistic locus where the souls of Israel are rooted
tmp:2734: "He is also the aspect of the Place of the world" (mekomo shel olam) — the theological principle that God contains the world rather than being contained by it
tmp:2735: "He drew His holiness there" — God's act of extending (himshikh) His kedushah into the Temple because of its beautiful things, without self-constriction
tmp:2737: "He alone, blessed be He, is fit to judge the world" — statement of God's exclusive prerogative as Judge on the Day of Judgment
tmp:2738: "Since He Himself, blessed be He, requests atonement then" — God's own plea 'bring an atonement for Me' on Rosh Chodesh (Chagigah motif) that emboldens Israel
tmp:2739: "We have no shame on the Day of Judgment to ask atonement" — the state of unashamed petitioning on Rosh Hashanah enabled by God's own request for kapparah
tmp:2740: God's fixing of the Day of Judgment, Rosh Hashanah, on Rosh Chodesh — a divine act of chesed in calendar design
tmp:2741: "Raising our faces to ask atonement from Him" — the act of daring to petition God for kapparah, made possible by His kindness
tmp:2742: "They are all borrowers from him" — the supernal ministers and heavenly host as debtors ('all the stars borrow from one another') to one who grasps the root, the word of Hashem/prayer
tmp:2743: "Their brazenness falls before him" — the collapse of the unholy azut of falsely famous leaders before the master of prayer
tmp:2744: The ability to recognize the falsely famous leaders (mefursamim) whose renown comes through brazenness (azut) — a discernment granted by attaining prayer
tmp:2745: "When a person prays about some illness" — the act of petitionary prayer directed at a specific sickness (context of healing through dvar Hashem)
tmp:2747: Being healed through the word of Hashem (dvar Hashem) — healing drawn from the supernal root rather than from herbal remedies
tmp:2748: Dvar Hashem — 'the word of the Lord' as the supernal root of all creation ('by the word of Hashem the heavens were made'), identified with prayer
tmp:2749: Departing from the three servitudes (avodot) — exiting the three evil traits (idolatry/lust for money, sexual desire, gluttony) as the means of rectifying prayer
tmp:2751: The capacity to be healed through anything in the world — even bread and water — once prayer is perfected ('bakol mitrap'in', Pesachim 25)
tmp:2752: The condition of being 'outside' the three servitudes — the exclusion clause 'except idolatry, sexual immorality, and bloodshed' read as freedom from the three traits
tmp:2753: Exiting the three traits (money-lust, sexual desire, gluttony) — the state of departure from the three middot that permits universal healing
tmp:2754: "Through anything one may be healed — even with bread and water" — Talmudic dictum (Pesachim 25) reread as healing via ordinary food blessed from the root
tmp:2755: Grasping the root — dvar Hashem, the aspect of prayer — holding fast to the supernal source from which bread and water receive blessing and healing power
tmp:2758: Prayer as the aspect of dvar Hashem — tefillah identified with the creative word of God, attained through prophecy (navi as acronym of 'bidvar Hashem shamayim na'asu')
tmp:2759: The redemption and ransoming of prayer (ge'ulat ha-tefillah) — prayer's liberation from exile/disrespect, which topples all medicine
tmp:2760: The fall of all doctoring (doktorai) — the collapse of physicians and the needlessness of remedies once prayer is redeemed
tmp:2761: Prayer in its completeness (tefillah bi-shleimut) — the perfected state of prayer through which one heals via dvar Hashem in all things
tmp:2762: Prayer redeemed from exile — the freeing of tefillah from its degraded, despised state ('kerum zulut') via the flow of prophecy
tmp:2763: Hashpa'at ha-nevuah — the flow/effluence of prophecy present in the world (even without an actual prophet), which redeems prayer
tmp:2765: The angel created through building Jerusalem (perfected fear in the heart) that channels prophecy to the vessels of prophecy (the Cherubim, anpei zutrei)
tmp:2766: Sukkot — the festival of Tabernacles, one of the Three Festivals, at which the desire for eating/food is rectified
tmp:2767: The rectification of the desire for eating (ta'avat akhilah) — repair of gluttony effected through the festival (Sukkot) among the Three Festivals
tmp:2768: The rectification of sexual desire (ta'avat mishgal) — repair of carnal lust effected through the festival (Shavuot) among the Three Festivals
tmp:2770: The mitzvah of the Three Pilgrimage Festivals (shalosh regalim: Pesach, Shavuot, Sukkot) — commandment through which the three evil traits are rectified
tmp:2771: Meriting to rectify the three traits (money-lust, sexual desire, gluttony) — the attainment achieved through the Three Festivals
tmp:2772: "On each festival of the Three Festivals" — each individual regel as an occasion of renewed da'at/mochin rectifying one trait
tmp:2773: Rectifying these three traits — the tikkun of the three middot accomplished by drawing da'at into the heart ('know today and take it to your heart')
tmp:2774: Milk of a kosher animal (chalav kesherah) — permitted milk symbol in the three-watches homily, contrasted with nursing from impurity (context of the woman nursing in the third watch)
